title: Nine Inches of China
subtitle: 碗与餐具 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 碗与餐具（生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：碗与餐具（生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：bowl　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bowl 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my mother was sent to wash ① a bowl she could not fill, and she said the filling was the whole of the lesson. The ② bowl, meaning the china and not the soup, was nine inches wide and was carried by whoever came last; a bowl, she said, is the only thing in a cupboard that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ bowl in that cupboard had the same rim, and the ④ bowl at the back, meaning the one the cook kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever washed properly. A bowl, my grandmother said, is nine parts china and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the china is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bowl was the whole of the dinner, meaning the meal it held and not the china. The ⑥ bowl, meaning the dinner and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody passes and nobody questions; a bowl, he said, is either something you wash or the only word that means both a china and a dinner. She said the dinner is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ bowl had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the china. The ⑧ bowl of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine inches of china and eleven years of washing; a bowl, she said, is either the one at the back or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ bowl I remember is the one at the back, which was mended in 1972 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ bowl, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being filled; every bowl, she said, is a dinner that has agreed to look like a china. She said the dinner was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 碗（指瓷器本身，与汤相对）
C. 固定搭配：wash a bowl 洗一只碗
D. n. 碗（指柜子里每一只）
E. n. 碗（指后面那一只）
F. n. 碗（抽象：它所盛的那一餐）
G. n. 那一餐（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bowl she could not fill
The bowl, meaning the china and not the soup
bowl was the whole of the dinner
the bowl had become a photograph in a report
The bowl of the whole thing
A bowl, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: wash a bowl 意为“洗一只碗”，1948 年母亲被派去洗一只她盛不满的碗。
bowl 意为“碗”，指瓷器本身而不是汤，宽九英寸，由最后走的人端走。
bowl 指柜子里每一只碗，每一只都是同样的碗沿。
bowl 指后面那一只（厨子留的那一只），是唯一有人认真洗过的。
bowl 意为“碗”，抽象指它所盛的那一餐，父亲说 bowl 就是那顿晚饭的全部。
bowl 为抽象用法，指那一餐本身，是屋子里人人都传递、却没人质疑的东西。
bowl 意为“碗、钵”，到 1968 年这只 bowl 成了报告里的一张照片。
bowl 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸的瓷器和十一年的清洗。
bowl 意为“碗”，我记得的是后面那一只，1972 年补过，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
bowl 为抽象总称，祖母说碗是唯一会因为被盛满而变好的东西。
